answer: Every long voyage through the agent economy is charted on a shared atlas: before an identity vouches for a newcomer, it logs the route — which peers introduced it, at which epochs, against which stakes. The atlas acts as a mirror: anyone can replay the path and see if the chain of introductions holds or was fabricated after the fact. A vouch resting on a forged leg voids all downstream endorsements, and the forger pays 9,000 POA per fake identity, while honest charters whose voyages verify pay nothing and keep full vouching rights.
